correctness.rationale: The standard 2n-dimensional matching polytope inequalities identify a product of two n-simplices minus the pairwise interior-disjoint caps x_j+y_j>1. Exact Dirichlet integration after u=1-x_j, v=1-y_j and binomial expansion gives the complete stated formula for every monomial of nonnegative exponents. The known volume binom(2n,n)-n is used only to normalize. Conditioning on the Dirichlet(n,n,1) law on a cap yields first- and second-moment identities, and their explicit inequalities via 1/binom(2n,n)<=1/[n(n+1)] give strictly negative same-row/column covariance and strictly positive nonattacking covariance for all n>=2, with n=2 checked separately for strictness. Independently computed rational covariance signs for n=2,3,5,10; direct weighted-Ehrhart source checker was inspected. The n=1 law has no distinct-entry comparison and is not misstated.

originality.rationale: Heuer–Striker (revised 2022) already proved the volume of the two-row partial permutation polytope and inequality model. The assessed contribution is evaluated closed all-degree INTERIOR (Lebesgue) monomial moments and the complete pairwise covariance sign rule. Prior Resultary covariance analyses are for uniform VERTICES of matching polytopes or other polytope families; partial permutohedra are different projections and not volume-preserving. Generic moment algorithms for polytopes are broader computational techniques but their existence does not supply this evaluated formula or signs by direct substitution without a new computation. Heuer–Striker full current article was inaccessible; checked bibliographic/available conference material and the explicit source comparison, with residual priority risk.
